clue.text: Billiard-ball, badly cued, is potted

parts.note: a red is one of the coloured balls on a snooker or billiard table

indicators.note: a badly made shot here signals the four letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A snooker player mis-cues yet the ball still drops into the pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges CUED into UCED, placed after RED. 'potted' looks like a snooker word but means shortened, as in a potted history.
explanation.definitionFit: A potted version of something is an abridged or cut-down one, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Arch supporter of a bridge bid?

definitions.meaning: in architecture, a half-pillar against a wall bearing one end of an arch
in contract bridge, a call answering a partner's opening

explanation.definitionFit: It names both a pier taking an arch's weight and, as a verb, to reply to a partner at cards.

clue.text: Music from the cat's-cradle, say?

parts.note: a jazz cat is a musician; the cradle of jazz cats is the American South and its New Orleans style

explanation.definitionFit: Traditional jazz from New Orleans is named after the southern states, the birthplace of jazz.

clue.text: 8'4" certainty

parts.note: eight feet four inches makes one hundred, and C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
the measurement is all in one unit, so the other piece is the word for that unit, a twelfth of a foot

explanation.surface: A height measurement given as a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 feet 4 inches is 100 inches, read as C (Roman 100) followed by INCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinch is informal for something sure or easy, a dead cert.

clue.text: This piece of chicken may be battered

definitions.text: This piece of chicken may be battered

parts.words: This piece of chicken may be battered
parts.note: a chicken leg may be coated in batter, but the stick that strikes a drum is what batters

explanation.definitionFit: The lower leg of a fowl and the stick for beating a percussion instrument share the name.

clue.text: Scribble score

definitions.meaning: to scrawl or make a rough mark on a surface
to cut a line or groove into a surface

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are a quick mark made on something: a hurried scrawl and an incised line.

clue.text: Dodgy fish with wriggly tail

parts.note: a shad is a fish of the herring family

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, here of wriggly

explanation.surface: A suspicious-looking fish with a squirming tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dodgy is suspect or disreputable, of questionable honesty.

clue.text: Preparation for the night?

parts.note: suggests getting ready for bed, but means practice ahead of a show's opening night

explanation.definitionFit: A practice run of a play is the readying for its first performance.

clue.text: Language of many in extremity in India

definitions.text: Language of many in extremity in India

indicators.note: the many letter goes inside the word for extremity

parts.note: a tail is an extremity, the end part
M is the Roman numeral 1000, so stands for many

explanation.surface: The tongue spoken by millions at the southern tip of India.
explanation.walkthrough: Tamil is spoken in Tamil Nadu at India's southern extremity, so the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Dravidian tongue of southern India and Sri Lanka, spoken by tens of millions.

clue.text: Undergo water treatment for persistent trouble with toe-ends

parts.note: a hydra is a problem that keeps coming back, like the many-headed monster

indicators.note: the first and last letters of toe are taken

explanation.surface: Someone takes a spa cure for a nagging toe complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hydra grew two heads for each one cut off, hence a persistent trouble; 'ends' gives T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To combine chemically with water, or take it up, is to undergo that treatment.

clue.text: Low German weapon held by boy

indicators.note: the boy's word grips the weapon's letters between its own

parts.note: a son is a boy
an ax (axe) is a weapon

explanation.surface: A lad clutches a weapon, described in a German-language phrasebook.
explanation.definitionFit: Low Saxon is a variety of Low German, so the regional name stands for that language.

clue.text: Bold nude, disturbed, swallows a humbug

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take the next pieces inside them as if gulping them down
the letters of the word nude are disturbed, set into a different order

parts.note: a humbug is a fraud or sham

explanation.surface: A brazen nudist, upset, gulps down a mint sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' turns NUDE into UNED, and 'swallows' puts A plus SHAM inside it: UN-A SHAM-ED. A humbug is also a British boiled mint sweet, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bold in this sense is shameless, feeling no embarrassment.

clue.text: Reckless fast bowling to open

indicators.note: the cricket word is placed so that it opens, coming before the other piece

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
hasty means quick or fast

explanation.surface: A cricket captain rashly brings on his quick bowler to open the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a spell of six deliveries in cricket; 'to open' puts it at the front of HASTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting far too hurriedly without thought is rash, impetuous behaviour.

clue.text: Each and every duck at a place in Scotland

parts.note: all means each and every one
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Every single duck is found at a Scottish location.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLOA is a town in central Scotland on the River Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a Clackmannanshire town, so it is an example of a Scottish locality.

clue.text: Stunt employed by cold war faction

indicators.note: the run of letters is used within, spanning the words cold war faction

explanation.surface: A publicity gimmick used by one side in the Cold War.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across colD WAR Faction. 'Stunt' looks like a noun for a publicity trick but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To stunt growth is to keep something undersized, which is what it means to make it a midget version.

clue.text: Show-circus, about end of July, leaves marks on the grass

indicators.note: the show and circus words surround the letter, coming about it

parts.note: a fair is a show or exhibition
a ring is a circus arena

indicators.note: the last letter of July is wanted

explanation.surface: A circus show at the close of July leaves its marks on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts Y (end of July) between FAIR and RING.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle of darker grass or mushrooms on a lawn, caused by fungus, is folklore's dancing ground of elves.

clue.text: Pottery found in golf clubs with style

parts.note: irons are a class of golf clubs
tone can mean style or character, as in the tone of a place

explanation.surface: Some china is discovered among a golfer's kit, done with flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironstone china is a hard, durable type of earthenware made in Staffordshire.

clue.text: Unknown number in hydro, too abnormal for conformism

indicators.note: the unknown goes inside the rearranged letters
abnormal means not in the usual form, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: x is the conventional unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A mysterious figure in a spa hotel is too unusual for conventional tastes.
explanation.walkthrough: A hydro is a hotel offering water cures. 'abnormal' rearranges HYDROTOO, and X goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherence to accepted beliefs or practices is conventionality, the opposite of heresy.

clue.text: Total of those dismissed may be more

definitions.meaning: in cricket, the count of batsmen given out

explanation.definitionFit: Split, it is the count of outs; whole, it means to exceed in quantity.

clue.text: CD mike with endless trouble in the "on" position

indicators.note: to trouble is to stir up, so the gathered letters are thrown into disorder
the word with loses its final letter, having no end

explanation.surface: A broadcaster struggles with a faulty CD and microphone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts WITH to WIT; 'trouble' rearranges CDMIKE and WIT. The 'on' side in cricket is the leg side, where midwicket is a fielding position.
explanation.definitionFit: Midwicket is a fielding place on the leg side of a cricket field, also called the on side.

clue.text: Fellow leaves tropical fruit

parts.note: a fellow is a man
leaves means goes away, departs

explanation.surface: A chap departs, leaving foliage on exotic fruit trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: These are juicy stone fruits grown in hot climates such as India.

clue.text: Ignited high explosive in limber

parts.note: lit means set alight

explanation.surface: An explosive is set off inside a gun carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: A limber is also the detachable front of a gun carriage, which the explosives surface plays on; here it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Limber and the answer both describe a body that is supple and bends easily.

clue.text: Record on green-turning table-centre

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: turning signals the letters of green are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A record spins on a green turntable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges GREEN into ERGNE, placed after EP; 'on' means after in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is an ornamental centrepiece for a dining table, with dishes for fruit or flowers.

clue.text: Never in the country outside King's Cross, say?

indicators.note: the dialect word sits around the king's letter, outside it

parts.note: nary is a rural dialect form meaning not one or never
K is the abbreviation for king, in chess notation

explanation.surface: A traveller insists they never go anywhere near King's Cross station.
explanation.walkthrough: King's Cross is a major London railway station; 'Cross' is wrenched away to be the definition, with 'say' marking it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Narky is British slang for irritable, so it is one way of being in a bad mood.

clue.text: Teacher's pet, practically

indicators.note: practically means almost, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rabbit is a common pet

explanation.surface: The classroom favourite, nearly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teacher's pet' looks like a set phrase; the 's is 'is'. 'practically' drops the last letter of RABBIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious scholar and instructor.

clue.text: Way of acting by method?

parts.note: read as theatre it hints at Method acting, but plainly it is the established manner of doing something by fixed steps

explanation.definitionFit: It is the set series of steps followed in carrying out a task, a course of action.

clue.text: Quiet country road in Lincoln, for example

parts.note: p, piano, means quiet in music
a lane is a narrow country road

explanation.surface: A quiet lane in the cathedral city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: The Avro Lincoln was a British bomber aircraft; Lincoln looks like the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lincoln was a Second World War-era bomber, so it is an example of an aircraft.

clue.text: Award five hundred — enough for poet to carry

indicators.note: the poetic word carries the numeral inside it

parts.note: enow is an archaic, poetic form of enough
D is the Roman numeral 500

explanation.surface: A prize of five hundred pounds is plenty for a poet to bear.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to bestow or give funds or a quality, so it means to grant.

clue.text: A big lob turns out to become an essential part of the score

definitions.text: an essential part of the score

indicators.note: the letters turn out differently, being reworked into new order

explanation.surface: A high tennis lob proves decisive in the match score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges A BIG LOB into OBBLIGA, and TO follows as written. 'score' looks like a sporting tally but is a piece of written music.
explanation.definitionFit: In music an obbligato is an accompanying instrumental part that must not be omitted.

clue.text: Girl coming out, under guarantee initially, to repair computer

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a girl making her entrance into society

indicators.note: only the opening letters of under and guarantee are taken

explanation.surface: A young society girl, still in warranty, fixes the computer.
explanation.walkthrough: A debutante 'comes out' into high society; DEB is followed by U and G.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove faults from software or a machine is to fix its errors.

clue.text: Horse in one run requires a gravelly beach

indicators.note: the drug letter goes inside the cricket word

parts.note: a single is one run in cricket
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A racehorse in one race needs a stony seashore.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is the mass of small rounded pebbles making up a stony shore.

clue.text: Bowmen were yet ordering wood from it

definitions.text: Bowmen were yet ordering wood from it

indicators.note: the letters of were and yet are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Archers were still placing orders for timber taken from a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordering' rearranges WERE and YET. Longbows were traditionally made from yew wood, so the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: English longbows were cut from the wood of this conifer, so archers sourced their timber from it.
